fact.thing: tax on a $5,000 TFSA overcontribution left in for six months
fact.claim: When your TFSA holds more than your contribution room, the CRA charges a tax of 1% per month on the highest excess amount in the account in each month. The tax keeps applying every month until you withdraw the whole excess or new contribution room in later years absorbs it. A $5,000 excess left in for six months costs $5,000 × 1% × 6 = $300. A month still counts even if you put the excess in and take it out within that same month.

plain.what: A TFSA is a savings or investing account where your gains are not taxed, but it has a yearly limit on how much you can put in. If you put in more than your limit, the CRA (the tax office) charges you 1% of the extra amount every month. Putting in $5,000 too much and leaving it there for six months costs $300.
plain.so_what: That $300 comes straight out of your own money, and the charge keeps coming every month until the whole extra amount is out or new room in a later year covers it.
plain.do: Look up how much TFSA room you have left, then add up everything you have put in this year.
